named_partner_consumed.applied_result: Exact autonomous-chain deletion corridor law W_C(tau)=binom(|C|+K(tau),K(tau)) and boundary-active reduction; used to retain exact deletion multiplicities rather than assume a uniform quotient law.

new_result.statement: For any incomparable a,b and any linear extension tau of P\{a,b}, admissible insertion gaps I_a,I_b give exact fiber counts A_tau=#{i<j}+|I_a cap I_b| and B_tau=#{i>j}+|I_a cap I_b|. Therefore p(a<b)>2/3 forces some exact deletion fiber with A_tau>2 B_tau.
new_result.width_three_bridge: The set of elements incomparable with both a and b is a chain; in common-left nested fibers an extreme A_tau>2B_tau requires 2(|I_b|-|I_a|)>|I_a|+1.
new_result.adversarial_test: An exact width-three 8-element poset with 121 extensions has a first-boundary Hasse fork and earliest sibling distinguisher for which every local incomparable pair remains extreme, refuting local closure; the next span pair 6<2 has probability 66/121 and is balanced.

next_obligation: Prove a span-propagation lemma: in a minimal width-three counterexample, an extreme first-fork sibling fiber A_tau>2B_tau cannot remain compatible with extreme adjacent majority boundaries through the first profile distinguisher. Use the common-neutral-chain fact plus boundary-active corridor structure; the 121-extension adversary shows one fork plus one distinguisher is insufficient.
